text:
Russia is the largest country in the world, but honestly, Aunt May’s living room was the only territory worth conquering that week. Her knitting club, affectionately known as "Stitch and Bitch," was supposed to be a place for polite chatter and wool, not a crime scene investigation. The real headline of the evening wasn’t the neighborhood drama; it was the feline fugitive who had decided that unraveling a brand-new sweater was a better use of time than napping.

The result was a trail of woolly breadcrumbs stretching from the armchair to the kitchen, so extensive that Hansel and Gretel would have been envious of the navigation system. You couldn’t take a step without sinking into a soft, gray swamp of yarn. It was the ultimate relatable nightmare: you’re trying to maintain a dignified posture while sitting on a pile of your own hard work, wondering if you should call the police or just accept that your cat has successfully turned your home into a giant, fuzzy ball pit.
